findings.title: No dependency manifest
findings.detail: No requirements.txt, environment.yml, pyproject.toml or Dockerfile. The environment cannot be rebuilt from the release, so version drift is guaranteed.

findings.title: No executable entry point
findings.detail: No __main__ guard, CLI parser or conventional entry script (train.py, eval.py, ...). There is nothing obvious to run.

findings.title: No README
findings.detail: There is no README, so the mapping from paper sections to commands is undocumented.

findings.title: No random-seed control
findings.detail: Nothing in the repository fixes random, numpy or framework seeds, so a re-run samples a different point in the training distribution and the reported number cannot be reproduced exactly.

findings.title: README does not say how to install or run
findings.detail: No pip/conda/make invocation was found in the README, so the intended environment and command are left to the reader to guess.

findings.title: No configuration file; hyperparameters are hard-coded
findings.detail: No YAML/JSON/TOML config or hparams module was found, so the paper's hyperparameters have to be reverse-engineered from source code edits.

findings.title: No tests
findings.detail: Nothing verifies the implementation against known-good behaviour, so a silent bug in the pipeline looks exactly like a reproduction failure.

findings.title: No licence file
findings.detail: Without an explicit licence the code is all-rights-reserved by default, which blocks reuse and redistribution even when it runs.
